# WS-engine-security — Group C security checks (owner: opencode lead)

**Own:** new files `packages/engine/src/checks/<id>.ts`, `packages/engine/test/<id>.test.ts`, and the array in `packages/engine/src/checks/security.ts`. Do not edit `types.ts`, `registry.ts`, `diffGuard.ts`, `secrets.ts`.

Copy the pattern of `checks/secrets.ts`. Each check implements `Check` from `types.ts`. Detectors are pure TypeScript over `ctx.repo.files` (in-memory text). Never execute repo code. Fixers are deterministic templates (no AI), return a `Patch`, and **must recompute from `ctx.repo`** because earlier patches may have changed the files (do not trust finding line numbers). Every patch must pass `guardPatch` from `diffGuard.ts`: additive patches may only add lines and create new files; `minimal-edit` patches must list each removed line in `allowedRemovals`. Generated helper files use **no new npm dependencies** in the user's app.

Express detection: find the file containing `express()` assigned to a variable (`const app = express();`); insert new lines right after that line.

Checks to build (id → behaviour):
1. `security-headers` (high, auto): fail if no helmet import and no code setting `Content-Security-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options`. Fix (additive): create `security.js` exporting `(app) => app.use((req,res,next)=>{ set CSP default-src 'self', X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, Strict-Transport-Security; res.removeHeader('X-Powered-By'); next(); })` and insert `require('./security')(app);` after the app line (use ESM `import` form if the file is ESM).
2. `rate-limit` (high, auto): fail if `/login`, `/signup`, `/register`, `/reset` routes exist and no limiter (`rateLimit`, `express-rate-limit`, `limiter`). Fix (additive): create `rateLimit.js` (in-memory fixed window per IP, 5 req / 15 min default via env, 429 JSON) and insert `app.use(['/login','/signup','/register','/reset'], require('./rateLimit')());` after the app line.
3. `open-cors` (medium, auto): fail on `Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*'` or `cors()` with no options or `origin: '*'`. Fix (minimal-edit): replace `'*'` with `process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGIN || 'http://localhost:3000'` on that one line.
4. `auth-on-endpoints` (critical, auto): parse `app|router.(get|post|put|patch|delete)('<path>', ...handlers)`. Fail for routes under `/admin` (or `/api/admin`) whose handler list has no name matching `/auth|admin|protect|requireLogin|isLoggedIn|verify/i` and no prior `app.use('/admin', ...)`. Fix (additive): create `auth.js` exporting `requireAdmin` (checks `Authorization: Bearer <token>` against `process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN`, 401 otherwise; comment that Cognito JWT replaces this in production) and insert `app.use('/admin', require('./auth').requireAdmin);` after the app line.
5. `sql-string-concat` (critical, report): flag `prepare|query|exec|run|all|get(` calls whose first argument concatenates a string literal containing SQL keywords (`SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|WHERE`) with `+` or a template `${}`. Report-only; `explanation` must show the parameterised version (`?` placeholder + argument).
6. `dependency-audit` (high, auto): read `package-lock.json` (lockfileVersion 2/3 `packages` map; `node_modules/a` = direct-or-hoisted, `node_modules/a/node_modules/b` = nested), mark direct deps from `package.json`. Query OSV.dev `POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/querybatch` with `{queries:[{package:{name,ecosystem:"npm"},version}]}` using `ctx.fetch ?? fetch`, then `GET https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id>` for details (severity, summary, `affected[].ranges[].events[].fixed`). One finding per vulnerable package with `evidence` = `name@version → fixed in X (GHSA/CVE id)` and whether direct or transitive with its chain. Fix (minimal-edit): for direct deps only, bump the version in `package.json` to `^<lowest fixed version>` (one line per package, listed in `allowedRemovals`); reason must say "verified only after npm install + tests pass in CI". Tests must mock `fetch` (no network in tests). If OSV is unreachable, throw so the check shows as errored, never as passed.

Tests: for each check, one failing fixture repo → detect finds it; one clean fixture → no findings; fix → `applyPatch` succeeds (guard OK) → re-detect returns `[]`. Also one test that applies all security fixers in sequence on one Express fixture and the guard accepts every patch.

Done when `npm test -w @siidekick/engine` passes and `npx tsc -p packages/engine/tsconfig.json` has no errors.
